channel.title: Morning Education
channel.description: Delivered every Monday by 10 a.m., Weekly Education examines the latest news in education politics and policy.

item.title: Why the GOP’s student loan payback push could be a problem
item.description: The White House is trying to get a handle on rising costs eating into household budgets. But Republicans aren't as flexible when it comes to student loans.
item.dc:creator: By Rebecca Carballo and Mackenzie Wilkes
item.dc:contributor: By Rebecca Carballo and Mackenzie Wilkes

item.title: Supreme Court to wade into debate over religious schools — again
item.description: The Supreme Court is set to hear yet another case involving public funding for religious schools — and the clash between free exercise and state policies guarding against discrimination.
item.dc:creator: By Bianca Quilantan

item.title: Trump’s anti-American Bar Association push could split states
item.description: The Trump administration is trying to cut ties with the American Bar Association. A slew of red states might be next to part ways with the legal group.
item.dc:creator: By Rebecca Carballo

item.title: Trump vs. Harvard fires up
item.description: The Trump administration and Harvard University are going toe to toe in appeals court this week over federal research grants and enrollment of international students.
item.dc:creator: By Isa Domínguez

item.title: Trump changes prompt fears of racial discrimination in schools
item.description: The Trump administration is rewriting the rules of civil rights enforcement, ending a decades-old legal framework that had been used to protect students of color against unintentional discrimination.
item.dc:creator: By Bianca Quilantan

item.title: A Democratic plan to save the Education Department
item.description: Trump administration officials are feeling good their efforts to dismantle the Education Department so far. A blue wave in the midterms could put a stop to that.
item.dc:creator: By Rebecca Carballo

item.title: The latest plans that could shake up education funding
item.description: Schools and colleges could face more funding uncertainty under a new proposal from the Education Department.
item.dc:creator: By Mackenzie Wilkes

item.title: What college presidents find ‘frightening’ about Trump’s latest moves
item.description: College presidents say they are watching the Trump administration’s latest higher education actions with a mix of alarm and caution.
item.dc:creator: By Bianca Quilantan

item.title: What’s the real cost of college?
item.description: The Trump administration wants to change how students can compare college offers as tuitions keep rising.
item.dc:creator: By Rebecca Carballo
